scope: Selected workflows from the current manuscript, not an exhaustive classification or an empirical ranking.
columns: PDE residual / solver in online loop

legend.0: Not part of the depicted workflow, not an impossibility claim

rows.name: Direct inverse maps
rows.reason: Selected deterministic maps reuse a trained predictor. Tandem training uses a forward surrogate, but deployment does not require a PDE solve. Probabilistic inverse maps are separate variants.

rows.name: PDE-residual optimization
rows.reason: Instance-specific residual fitting uses measurements or design/control targets and the PDE. The depicted configuration does not require a labeled parameter/solution training set. Amortized solver-trained controllers are not represented by this row.

rows.name: Forward-surrogate optimization
rows.reason: Depicts a fixed data-trained surrogate queried by an optimizer. Physics-informed surrogate training and hybrid solver corrections are alternative setups. Feedback is present in MPC variants, including the cited Koopman control example. Neural adjoint also provides general inverse-problem background.

rows.name: Visual inverse dynamics
rows.reason: IFD couples a differentiable Euler simulator and volume rendering in instance-specific video reconstruction. Temporal fitting is not feedback control.

rows.name: Generative posterior inference
rows.reason: The selected diffusion workflow uses a pretrained joint field prior with observation and PDE-residual guidance. Iterative sampling can produce multiple candidates, without a blanket calibration guarantee.

rows.name: Generative inverse design
rows.reason: CinDM composes learned joint energy models and performs iterative sampling for candidate designs. Independent CFD validation after generation is not counted as physics in the online generation loop.

rows.name: Operator-based feedback
rows.reason: Neural gain operators replace repeated kernel solves. The underlying feedback controller still uses the observed state. Integration and policy evaluation are not iterative online optimization.

rows.name: Imitation control
rows.reason: Depicts observation-to-action behavioral cloning such as the Burgers PDE control baseline in DiffPhyCon Appendix H.4 (PDF page 37). Demonstrations need not be optimal. Data generation can itself be expensive. Sequence-level open-loop imitation is outside this row.

rows.name: Generative control
rows.reason: Generative control uses iterative trajectory sampling. Feedback requires a suitable variant, illustrated by CL-DiffPhyCon. Objective guidance is not itself a full PDE solve.

rows.name: Reinforcement learning
rows.reason: Depicts a trained observation-to-action policy. Simulator interactions occur during learning, and deployed policy evaluation does not require an online PDE solve. Model-based planning is a different setup.
